_comment: Mutations for the email template renderer. The Jinja templates themselves are shared with the Python — there is one copy on disk and both stacks load it — so what can drift is everything around them: which files escape, how they escape, and the two Python string methods minijinja does not have. The corpus in tests/fixtures/email_corpus.json is the only harness that can see any of it; the outbox rows these strings become are compared column by column by the write differential, so a render that differs by one entity is a real difference.

mutations.name: the escaper escapes the slash
mutations._why: minijinja's own escaper does. Every dashboard link in an email is full of slashes.

mutations.name: the escaper writes the apostrophe in hex
the escaper writes the quote as a named entity
the generic body escapes like markupsafe
mutations._why: The fallback body calls html.escape, not markupsafe.escape — the two disagree on the apostrophe and nothing else. Pins that they really are different functions.

mutations.name: a safe value is escaped on output
the escape filter escapes an already-escaped value
the text templates escape too
mutations._why: Autoescape is per file by the inner extension; a text body showing & would be wrong.

mutations.name: replace takes only the first occurrence
replace ignores its count
split caps at the wrong number
mutations._why: Python's maxsplit counts splits; splitn counts fields.

mutations.name: split drops its empty fields
trim_blocks is off
lstrip_blocks is off
the subject keeps an embedded CRLF
mutations._why: A camera name is operator-controlled and an incident title is agent-written; an embedded \r\nBcc: is a header injection the day a provider forwards subjects to SMTP raw.

mutations.name: the subject is not trimmed
the dashboard url keeps its trailing slash
meta is never parsed
a meta blob that is not an object is used anyway
mutations.equivalent: A list or a scalar reads as an empty mapping either way as far as the templates go — none of them reads a key called `value`, so wrapping the blob instead of dropping it changes no byte. The observable half of this branch is covered by `meta is never parsed`.

mutations.name: the warning colour is the healthy one
an error is not coloured like a critical
the layout is skipped
the generic text body omits the link
the generic text body links an empty path
mutations._why: Python tests `if notif.link`, so the empty string is as absent as None.

mutations.name: the generic html body does not escape
